metadata.title: When a screened pattern search spends more simulator calls: evidence from mineral-processing circuit cases
metadata.description:
Surrogate screening can add trial evaluations as well as avoid them. This study compares neural surrogate screening with an unscreened generalized pattern search on 72 paired target-mode variants from twelve authored mineral-processing circuit cases. Screening recorded 26,367 distinct cached trial states versus 22,487 without screening, a 17.25% increase (case-cluster bootstrap 95% interval 9.28 to 25.88%). Counts were higher in 68 variants, tied in four and lower in none. Terminal outcomes matched in 65 pairs; seven different feasible decisions differed by at most 0.0027 t/h in recovered metal. Of 5,811 exact-evaluated proposals, 901 improved an incumbent. Mean absolute recovery error was 0.71 percentage points (case-cluster interval 0.49 to 0.98), with a 38.16-point maximum. A separate twelve-case radius ablation recorded 3,683 evaluations without screening, 3,753 with one-step screening and 3,974 with one-and-two-step screening.

A filter-removal experiment on four selected authored cases recorded 1,007 evaluations without screening and 1,171 with the full policy. Removing the reconstruction guard did not change counts because it rejected no candidate in those runs. Removing the interval-width filter increased the count to 1,332; all policies returned the same exact endpoint decisions in this selected subset. These local results do not establish universal decision equivalence, global optimality, elapsed-time savings or performance on operating plants.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow
metadata.version_notes: Adds a completed four-case filter-removal study and regenerates the evidence figures and tables from persisted records. The reconstruction guard rejected no candidates in the selected subset, so its removal had no measured effect there; interval-filter removal increased exact proposals and cached evaluations. The paper states these subset limits and does not claim overall compute savings.
